sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Toledo?
sections.html:
Lucas County sends it, and the city does not. The County Auditor sets the value and the County Treasurer mails the bill. Both offices are in One Government Center downtown, the Auditor in Suite 600 and the Treasurer in Suite 500. The Auditor's line is 419-213-4406 and the Treasurer's is 419-213-4305. After the Treasurer collects, the Auditor sends the money out to every subdivision in the county.

Toledo's own Division of Taxation, in Suite 2070 of the same building, handles a different levy: the city income tax. Check the letterhead on anything that arrives. This page covers the county bill that attaches to a Toledo address.

Toledo has 263,423 people. Owners live in 53.3 percent of homes, the median value of an owner-occupied home is $114,500, and median gross rent is $901. With owners in just over half of homes, rentals shape many blocks. Treat those figures as a citywide midpoint, since a house in the Old West End historic district and one near the river can sit far from it. Older Toledo houses draw close looks at the roof, gutters and furnace from a buyer's inspector.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
The bill splits into two installments, due near the end of January and again near the end of July. Ohio bills a year in arrears, so a 2025 bill is paid in 2026. A mailed payment needs a postmark on or before the date, and web or phone payments made after 8:00 p.m. Eastern wait for the next business day. Money takes 5 to 7 days to show against your parcel.

The Treasurer cautions that postmarks now usually reflect the first machine pass, which may fall a day or more after you mail the envelope. Send it early, request a hand stamp at the post office window, or pick another channel.

sections.h2: The Inflation Cap Credit on your bill
sections.html:
It is a state-law reduction under R.C. 319.303 that appears as its own line labeled with those words. No application is needed, not every property gets it, and it is separate from both the homestead exemption and the owner-occupancy credit. The credit amount varies with property value, taxing district, school district and the taxes that qualify, and the Treasurer cannot adjust it.

Special assessments also ride on the bill after rollbacks. They cover snow and leaf removal, alleyway cleaning and sidewalk repair, among others, and they count as fees rather than taxes, so even tax-exempt parcels may owe them. Rates themselves come from levies voters passed. The basic math is 35 percent of market value multiplied by the district rate, followed by the rollbacks and credits. The owner-occupied credit and the homestead exemption apply after the House Bill 920 rollbacks.

sections.h2: Does the Toledo income tax matter when I sell?
sections.html: It matters only if you are a Toledo filer. The city's rate has been 2.5 percent since January 1, 2021 under Toledo Municipal Code 1905.011, and individual returns are due April 15. It is a separate bill from the county's real estate tax. Appointments with the Finance Department go through Engage Toledo at 419-936-2020. Engage Toledo is also the city's request channel for tall grass, blight and structure concerns, which is worth knowing before a showing if a lot has drawn complaints.

sections.h2: Lucas County steps before a Toledo closing
sections.html:
Three county tasks come up for most sellers:

  • Rental registration. Under R.C. 5323, any livable structure that is not your primary home must be registered as a rental or carry a filed exception, with fines possible otherwise. Look up an address in the Auditor's AREIS database.
  • Deed transfer. Staff at the Auditor's office are barred from drafting a deed. The Engineer's Tax Map Department on the seventh floor approves the legal description, the Recorder checks the fee amounts, and the Auditor on the sixth floor takes the conveyance form. Both buyer and seller attend with unexpired photo ID.
  • Fees. The conveyance fee is $4.00 per $1,000 of price with a $0.50 charge per parcel, and the deed recording fee is $39.00 for two pages and $8.00 for every page after.

Mobile home titles need all current-year taxes paid before transfer.

Plan the order. Get the deed prepared by an attorney or title company, have the Tax Map Department approve the description, take the conveyance form to the Auditor, and then record. Because both parties attend with photo ID, schedule the visit around both calendars.

sections.h2: When the tax on a Toledo house is behind
sections.html:
The Treasurer's Delinquent Installment Payment Plan lets an owner-occupant pay past-due tax over up to 24 months with 20 percent down. Plans are not issued in the ten days right after a due date. An exception request is answered in most cases within ten business days.

The county can also sell delinquent liens as tax certificates. A notice does not mean the house was sold, and the office generally keeps owner-occupied homes and homestead properties out of such sales. The Treasurer must give the record owner at least 30 days' written notice before a negotiated sale. The tax lien hotline is 419-574-6022. Separately, the Lucas County Land Bank, founded in 2010, works to return vacant and tax-delinquent properties to use.

If you plan to sell, ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure and have the title company pay it from your proceeds at closing. A cash buyer can often close quickly on a house with back taxes, but the balance still has to be cleared at settlement.

faqs.q: Does the City of Toledo bill my property tax?
faqs.a: No. Lucas County's Auditor values the house and the Treasurer bills it. The city collects income tax through its Division of Taxation.

faqs.q: How soon does a mailed Lucas County tax payment post?
faqs.a: Allow 5 to 7 days. Timeliness turns on the postmark, and the Postal Service may stamp the envelope a day or more after you drop it off, so mail well ahead of the due date.

faqs.q: Is the Inflation Cap Credit the same as homestead?
faqs.a: No. It is automatic under R.C. 319.303 and separate from the homestead exemption and owner-occupancy credit. Your bill shows it on its own line when it applies.

faqs.q: Must a Toledo rental be registered before I sell it?
faqs.a: Yes. Rentals belong in the Lucas County Auditor's registry, and a property that is not your primary home but is not a rental needs an exception on file. Skipping it may bring fines.

faqs.q: What is the Toledo city income tax rate?
faqs.a: It is 2.5 percent, in place since January 1, 2021. It is separate from the county real estate bill.
